title: How Dizzy Gillespie's bent horn happened
summary: The horn fell off the piano at Snooky's and was bent; the repairman said it would break, so Dizzy kept it.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: I was with Dizzy... You know where he got that idea of that horn?
The horn fell off the piano at Snooky's, and it bent it up.
So you said Dizzy's horn fell off the piano, huh?

Yeah, and bent it up. So he asked me to take it over to that horn repairman on Eighth Avenue. So I took the horn over there the next day. And the guy said, 'I can't fix this horn. If I bend it back, it's going to break.' So I took it back to Dizzy and I said, 'The man says it will break if he straightens it out.' So he just kept playing like that, and he fell in love with it shooting up like that. Then he had the horn come to the bill of the horn, with that...shooting up. That's how... That thing came about by accident.
Well, that's interesting. That's very interesting to know, Foots. You were there.
